tagline: Over the Green Mountains on US 4 and down the Ottauquechee.
intro: East of Rutland, whose marble quarries prospered once Carrara's had grown too deep to work, US 4 narrows to two lanes and climbs into the Green Mountains past Mendon to Sherburne Pass. Over the top it meets the Ottauquechee at Killington, where the river begins, and follows it down through Bridgewater and Woodstock to Quechee, then on to White River Junction and the New Hampshire line.
Killington's voters have twice chosen to leave Vermont and join New Hampshire, 25 miles east. The votes were symbolic. US 4 goes there anyway.

moments.title: Sherburne Pass
moments.text: The height of land between Pico Peak and Deer Leap Mountain, where water on the west side drains to Lake Champlain and the St. Lawrence and on the east to Long Island Sound.

moments.title: Taftsville Covered Bridge
moments.text: Floods took the bridges here in 1807, 1811 and 1828, and the covered bridge Solomon Emmons finished in 1836 still stands, reopened in 2013 after Hurricane Irene.

moments.title: Quechee Gorge
moments.text: From the US 4 bridge the Ottauquechee runs 165 feet below, at the bottom of the deepest gorge in Vermont, cut as the ice sheet withdrew some 13,000 years ago.
